info.title: HappyClaw API
info.description:
**HappyClaw** is a local-first, single-user AI assistant. All routes are served under `/api`.

## Authentication

HappyClaw runs as a single local owner on this machine. There is no login, session,
role, or bearer-token gate: every request is handled as that owner, and
`/api/setup/*` is available while the first-run wizard is still open.

The desktop shell keeps its local credential bound through `/api/auth/device/*`
(`register` records it, `token` exchanges it on cold start).

Multi-user endpoints from earlier releases (invites, roles, SSO/OIDC/OAuth, LDAP,
MFA, passkey) are retired and answer `404` with `SINGLE_USER_UNSUPPORTED`.

## Streaming chat

Dashboard live turns use **WebSocket** at `/api/agents/{agent_id}/chat/ws`. Send
`{"type":"user_turn", ...}` frames; the server replies with JSON chunks matching the
harness stream format, ending with `{"type":"done"}` or
`{"type":"error","message":"..."}`.

Text-type dashboard pushes (cron reminders, proactive care) also emit
`{"type":"dashboard_push", ...}` on `/api/notifications/ws` so the SPA can show a toast
even when the chat socket is not subscribed.

HITL resume still uses `POST /api/agents/{agent_id}/chat/hitl/resume` (SSE).

post.summary: Decide where Bao should dispatch a task
post.description:
Deterministic Router decision.

Bao only decides *where* work goes; execution stays with the target
conversation through ``/dispatch``. Matching order: explicit session title,
expert name, project name, then the most recent (preferably active)
conversation in scope. When the request is genuinely ambiguous we return
``needs_target`` with candidates instead of guessing. Only after the
deterministic chain asks for a target do we spend one lightweight model call
on a second opinion; if that is not confident either, ``needs_target`` stays.

delete.description:
Remove a conversation thread, its checkpoint data, and its metadata.

Checkpoint deletion runs first. ``CHECKPOINT_DELETE_FAILED`` leaves
the thread row in place so the caller can retry, instead of dropping
the only handle to data that is still on disk.

``compact=true`` rebuilds the SQLite file before the response returns,
so the file can shrink immediately. The expert pauses while that runs.
``compact=false`` only deletes the rows. It does not vacuum. Idle
maintenance reclaims the free space later, once the freelist is large
enough. Omitting ``compact`` keeps the previous empty 204.
